newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts see slower Veba earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see slower Veba earnings growth.

text.p: Analysts say that German utility giant Veba AG is unlikely to beat 1995's record earnings in 1996, and are cautious on the earnings outlook for Veba ahead of the release of its nine-month figures on Wednesday.

Pre-tax profits grew by nearly 50 percent in the first nine months of 1995, but analysts said the group had already enjoyed most of the benefits of restructuring and higher productivity and forecasted "normal" profit growth.

"We are forecasting sales of 54.7 billion marks in the first nine months of the year, only very slightly higher than the 54.55 billion mark figure in the same period last year," said Roland Pitz, utilities analyst at Hypo-Bank at Munich.
"Profit growth at Veba will be normal this year. We are forecasting pre-tax profits of 2.35 billion marks, while net profits will come out at 1.1 billion marks," said Pitz.
Earlier in the year, Veba's chief financial officer Kurt Lauk said in an interview that profits would rise by about 10 percent in 1996, depending on how the economy performed.
Group net profits are forecast to come out at 1995 levels, while pre-tax profit forecasts are set to come out 7.3 percent higher than the previous year.

"Our full-year forecast is for an EPS figure of 4.80 marks per share, which is in line with most other analysts' views. If the outcome is between 4.80 marks and five marks, the market won't be surprised," said Pitz.

Any earnings per share (EPS) figure over the five-mark-level will be viewed as a positive surprise by the market. If the EPS figure comes out below 4.70 marks, it will be bad for the share, Pitz said.
Much of the focus in the current year has been on Veba's fledgling telecommunications business, which is still a cost-centre for the group as it attempts to expand its interests in the sector.
Early in October, Veba said it was merging its German telecommunications activities with those of fellow utility RWE and British-based Cable & Wireless.
Analysts are hesitant to make any forecasts about Veba's telecoms business, as many of the group's statements about when the sector would reach break-even were made before the alliance with RWE.
One analyst said it was possible that certain areas could break even in 1998, but that others would take longer, depending on the capital expenditure involved.
